# v1.8.1 — Chrome shell frost correction

Date: 2026-09-14 (America/Los_Angeles).

## Scope and cause

CSS declaration ordering only, plus matching package versions and release
notes. No dependency, database migration, auth, API or deployment configuration
changes. Both images must carry 1.8.1. Existing production AI settings remain
unchanged; the same-day 1.8.0 catalogue audit and feature validation remain the
baseline. Dormant report infrastructure stays isolated as previously documented.

Production 1.8.0 served `index-CJFBoG8I.css` with only the prefixed header
backdrop declaration. Chrome computed `none` while Safari rendered the blur.
The Analytics date banner retained both declarations. A direct optimizer
experiment reproduced the loss and showed that placing the standard property
last preserves both. This avoids layout changes, opacity compensation, or a
dependency/build-configuration change.

## Local validation

- Four optimizer regression cases failed against the original CSS and passed
  after the fix: header, panel, sidebar, print reset.
- 16 focused tests passed: backdrop build, theme toggle, theme fallback.
- Frontend production build passed; existing large-bundle warning remains.
- Real frontend typecheck ratchet passed: 144 existing errors versus the
  stored ceiling of 148; no baseline file change.
- Served the optimized production build at `http://localhost:5173` with the
  real development backend at port 3001. Chrome's existing authenticated session
  opened Analytics. Both banners computed `blur(14px) saturate(1.5)` and the
  scrolled chart bars were visibly blurred in light and dark themes.
- The actual ARM64 frontend image also passed the Chrome localhost check at
  port 5173 with same-origin API routing. Its assets are `index-B_DQljr7.js`
  and `index-DIXHrdQx.css`; both blur declarations survived packaging.
- Safari's packaged localhost page was visually checked in light and dark
  themes after user interaction restored painting in its native automated
  view. Both banners retain the frosted effect.
- The user subsequently confirmed by direct visual inspection that the
  frosted glass is present in both Safari and Chrome on localhost.

## Published ARM64 images

Both images were built with `docker buildx --builder desktop-linux` using
`--platform linux/arm64`. No global builder/context switch or cleanup was used.
The frontend uses an empty `VITE_API_BASE_URL` for same-origin routing.

| `et2geiger/feed-frontend:1.8.1` | `sha256:ab9e1f897d596dd9fb5fa2f876ceaf72a0351b8751486bbf6d1e8590dee368f9` |

Backend runtime: Node 24.21.0, FEED 1.8.1; all 36 migrations applied to a
disposable database with external networking disabled. Frontend Nginx syntax
passed with the backend hostname resolved. The first isolated Nginx check had
no backend DNS and failed on that missing test fixture; the configured check
passed. Docker's desktop credential helper stalled; the existing macOS
credential helper published successfully using an isolated temporary client
configuration, without modifying saved Docker settings or credentials.

## Completed release and deployment procedure

1. Finish cross-browser checks, build versioned frontend/backend, and publish
   `v1.8.1` as the latest stable GitHub release.
2. Build and push the FEED Docker images; verify published image identities.
3. Through Raspberry Pi Connect screen sharing, inspect the existing checkout,
   Compose image resolution and healthy 1.8.0 containers.
4. Create a SQLite `.backup`, verify `integrity_check`, and archive storage and
   deployment environment/Compose files under a fresh pre-1.8.1 backup folder.
5. Fast-forward the Pi checkout, persist `VERSION=1.8.1` in `.env`, unset any
   shell VERSION override, and inspect resolved images before deploying only
   backend/frontend. Preserve Cloudflare Tunnel and persistent data.
6. Verify running image identities, health, Node runtime, WAL and 36 current
   migrations, then reload the public app and check version, release notes and
   scrolled header blur in Chrome and Safari.

Rollback: restore `.env` to `VERSION=1.8.0`, verify Compose resolution, and
recreate backend/frontend from retained 1.8.0 images. This patch adds no
migrations, so rollback does not require changing the database.

## Deployment status

Deployed September 14 at approximately 18:17 Pacific through Raspberry Pi
Connect's `feed-app-host` screen-shared terminal, using Computer. No SSH or
LOTTO host/repository operations were used.

- Preflight: healthy 1.8.0 services, checkout `d99f370`, 3.1 GB free, 254 MB
  database and 1.7 MB storage. Existing untracked `.env.bak-1.6.0`, backups and
  exports were preserved.
- Backup: `backups/2026-09-14-pre-1.8.1/production.db` was created with SQLite
  `.backup`; `integrity_check` returned `ok`. The storage archive passed
  `gzip -tv`; Compose and both environment files were copied into the
  restricted backup directory.
- Fast-forwarded to release commit `7962a00`, persisted `VERSION=1.8.1`,
  cleared the shell override and checked Compose's resolved images.
- Pulled and recreated only backend/frontend. Both are healthy, and their
  running image digests match the published manifests above. Cloudflare
  Tunnel retained its existing nine-day uptime.
- Backend reports Node 24.21.0, WAL mode and 36 completed migrations. Startup
  reports no pending migrations. Local and public `/health` both return
  `{"status":"ok","version":"1.8.1"}`.
- Chrome production loads `index-B_DQljr7.js` and `index-DIXHrdQx.css`, displays
  Version 1.8.1 and opens its release notes without an Unreleased heading.
  The breadcrumb banner computes `blur(14px) saturate(1.5)`; chart bars behind
  it are visibly softened in both light and dark themes. No browser console
  errors were observed during the check.
- Safari production displays Version 1.8.1. Animated Analytics cards appeared
  blank in native automation, so the final scrolled visual check was handed
  to the user. The user confirmed production visual inspection was complete
  and looked correct, closing the remaining manual verification.
- GitHub `v1.8.1` is the latest stable release. Docker `1.8.1` and `latest`
  tags share the respective manifest digests above. Release tag `v1.8.1`
  remains on `7962a00`; subsequent documentation records deployment evidence.

Rollback remains available from retained 1.8.0 images and the verified backup.
No production AI calls or key/model-setting changes were made.
The temporary local frontend test container was removed after validation;
Vite development is restored on port 5173 with the backend on port 3001.
